environment: Node 22.14 and local PostgreSQL 17.11 with disposable source and checkpoint fixtures
observations: The application runtime verified a signed ES256 token and live source session, then accepted a deletion through the public HTTP route.
The worker runtime rejected a mismatched issuer before erasure or provider work. With the correct issuer it used the modern Supabase key header, requested hard deletion and verified account absence.
The application exposed a completed receipt only after the separate HTTPS journal admitted the worker outcome and the observer acknowledged it.
A changed approval reference, wrong database OID and unresolved journal claim left acceptance unavailable. Processing disabled independently.
Authenticated worker status reported signed used and reserved counts, the 80 percent warning and unavailable authority state. Aggregate output excluded fixture identity and credentials.
scope: The provider and JWKS were simulated. Source, worker, roles, observer, PostgreSQL authority, TLS transport, JWT verifier and application HTTP routes were real local implementations.
The optional billing PostgreSQL unit skip is exercised in the wire suite.
Hosted source, keys, journal and provider were untouched. A usable lineage lifecycle, hosted restore, provider verification and alert delivery remain release work.
